cohort: 544 women with consecutive live singleton deliveries (>24 weeks of gestation) at the Edith Wolfson Medical Center, each with one IVF pregnancy matched to one natural pregnancy
finding: In a cohort of women with both IVF and naturally conceived pregnancies, there were no significant differences in obstetric and perinatal outcomes, including preterm birth, SGA, and PIH, between the two groups.
mod_finding: There were no differences in rates of cesarean delivery between pregnancies conceived via IVF and natural pregnancies in the same women.
birth_weight: Birth weight was slightly lower in IVF pregnancies.
